coach.heading: Coach — Technical
coach.body:
## Coach — Technical

The serve is objectively fixed. Double faults across the four sessions: 2, 1, 1, 0. First serve percentage from 62% to 68%. Every tracked measure moved the right direction and the last practice returned zero faults over fifty serves. In the same four entries she wrote "the worst part of my game right now," "serve fell apart," "serve was a disaster," and "still not there." One of these accounts is describing what happened. The other is describing what she felt while it was happening.

This is the felt-vs-actual gap named in Block 1 and traced through Block 2. It has now completed: mechanics recovered before her perception did. Any drill work on the serve motion at this point will feed the wrong loop. She does not need reps. She needs to see the numbers.

Backhand approach volley disappeared from her voice again this block, third block running. Confirm it is fixed or reinstate the drill.

**This block:** three-minute film of the last serving set (S12: 34/50 firsts in, zero faults), shown to her before the next session. No commentary. Let the metrics do the work.

psychologist.heading: Sport Psychologist — Mental
psychologist.body:
## Sport Psychologist — Mental

The trust-in-motion pattern reached full form this block. Every entry names the serve as failing while the numbers show it recovering. This is not a state problem you talk her out of; it is the internal feedback loop running on stored evidence from Blocks 1 and 2 while the new evidence from Block 3 has not been read. The technical fix has to be a perceptual one — see the coach's directive.

One shift worth naming: in S12 she noticed Maya's positioning and used it. First time in three blocks a tactical read appears in her voice as agency, not pattern-recognition-after-the-fact. Motor confidence is starting to lead again in a domain outside the serve. This is the leading indicator; the serve narrative will follow.

Entry state degraded sharply in S10 and S11: "haven't slept well in almost three weeks now, mood has been low, everything feels a bit gray." This is outside sport-psychology.

See a professional.

**This block:** at the end of every session, before writing the take-away, one sentence answering "what did the numbers actually show today?" No editing.

tactics.heading: Tactics Analyst — Strategy
tactics.body:
## Tactics Analyst — Strategy

The reactive default is breaking. In S11 she catches herself hitting to the opponent mid-first-set, corrects for the second, loses the habit in the third. In S12 she reads Maya cheating to the forehand side and immediately targets the backhand corner. This is the same underlying pattern the coach and psychologist name — perception starting to move ahead of action — expressed in tactical terms.

What changed is not the recognition, which was there in Block 2. What changed is the interval between recognition and correction. In Block 1 the default was invisible. In Block 3 she is seeing it in real time and acting on it, though not yet reliably under pressure (the third set collapse in S11 is where it still fails).

S10 doubles win off Rhea's net play was a partner-carried result, not a tactical read. Do not confuse it with the S11 and S12 progress.

**This block:** in the next three doubles matches, at every changeover, one out-loud sentence: "where has she been standing this game?" One question, out loud, does what silent intention cannot.
